findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (missing file, permission denied)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> and use .map_err(|e| IoError::Read { path: path.to_string(), source: e }) or similar typed error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (non-numeric value field) aborts the parser instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue { field: parts[1].clone(), source: e }) and propagate through Result

findings.problem: as u16 lossy width cast converts u32 parse result to u16, silently truncating values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value of 70000 parses as u32 successfully then silently wraps to 4464 instead of returning Overflow

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into Vec<String> -- if line has no comma, parts.len() == 1 and parts[1] will panic on line 19
findings.failure_mode: malformed input with missing comma causes index-out-of-bounds panic via parts[1]
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::InvalidLine { line: line.to_string() }) and bind (_, value_str) = ...

findings.problem: println! side effect in what should be a pure parsing pipeline -- logging leaks into the functional core
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot suppress logging output; pure functions with hidden I/O are untestable and have observable side effects
findings.fix: remove println! from the parser; if logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell that calls the pure parser

findings.problem: load_sessions performs raw I/O (fs::read_to_string) and parsing in a single function -- no functional/core / imperative shell split
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing logic cannot be unit-tested in isolation from filesystem side effects
findings.fix: split into parse_records(&[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure core) and load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, IoError> (shell that reads file and delegates to core)

findings.problem: Record uses pub String and pub u16 fields -- any caller can construct arbitrary name/value combinations
findings.failure_mode: empty names, zero values, or other domain-invalid records are constructible at any call site with no enforcement
findings.fix: make fields private, provide a fallible constructor (e.g., Record::new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError>) that validates invariants, and consider newtypes for name

findings.problem: raw primitives (String, u16) enter the domain struct without a parse boundary or smart constructor
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct invalid states directly without going through validation logic
findings.fix: parse at the boundary into newtypes and enum variants through fallible constructors; hide Record fields and provide Record::from_csv_line

findings.problem: load_sessions collects all records into Vec<Record> with no try_reserve, no max_items cap, and no upper bound on allocation
findings.failure_mode: a very large file causes unbounded heap allocation and potential OOM with no typed error
findings.fix: add max_items: usize parameter, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| ParseError::Allocation)?, enforce max_items before pushing each Record

findings.problem: collects split parts into Vec<String> unnecessarily -- creates per-line intermediate heap allocations
findings.failure_mode: wastes heap allocations on intermediate String copies when split_once + &str borrowing suffices
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...)?; let name = part0.trim(); let value_str = part1.trim(); parse directly

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no typed error -- all failures (I/O, parse, overflow, allocation) are expressed via panic
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot distinguish file-not-found from malformed data from out-of-range values from OOM
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> with variants I/O, Invalid, Overflow, Allocation, and define SessionError as a typed domain error enum

findings.problem: value field is u16 -- a primitive that carries no domain meaning; could be confused with other u16 quantities
findings.failure_mode: accidental mixing of value u16 with other u16 fields (e.g., count, id) at compile time
findings.fix: introduce a newtype Value(u16) with FromStr/Display impls and domain-specific constructors

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated or implied performance of load_sessions
no profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, cargo-flamegraph) for allocation patterns
no allocation analysis (e.g., #[global_allocator] tracking, or valgrind/dhat) for Vec growth
no command evidence: no cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy results reported
no second-ring evidence: no fuzz testing, property tests, or Miri runs for error paths
no command-level documentation of how the crate is built, tested, or benchmarked
residual_risk: Static review only -- no commands run. The crate has 5 BLOCKER findings (unwrap, lossy cast, unchecked indexing, hidden side effects, no pure core split), 5 MAJOR findings (no newtypes, no parse boundary, no bounded allocation, no error taxonomy, intermediate allocation), and 1 MINOR finding (primitive value type). Every error path panics. The code must be refactored to return Result with typed errors, split into pure core + shell, replace unwrap with map_err, replace as cast with try_from, add try_reserve with max_items cap, and remove println! from the parser. Missing benchmark, profiler, allocation, and second-ring evidence means performance claims cannot be verified.
